short: The designated heir of Henry I who fought a prolonged civil war for the English throne.
full:
Matilda, the daughter of Henry I, was briefly Holy Roman Empress through her first marriage before being designated her father's heir to the English throne. Following Henry's death in 1135, her cousin Stephen of Blois usurped the crown. Matilda launched a prolonged military campaign from her stronghold in the West Country to reclaim her inheritance, plunging England into the Anarchy.

Though she captured Stephen and briefly held London in 1141, assuming the title 'Lady of the English', she was driven from the capital before she could be crowned queen. The conflict eventually deadlocked, and Matilda withdrew to Normandy in 1148. She never ruled England in her own right, but her relentless campaigning ensured that the crown ultimately passed to her son, Henry II, founding the Plantagenet dynasty.
